brief.t: Founded in Mumbai in 1919 by Seth Sitaram Poddar; Mahatma Gandhi inaugurated its head office building in 1921.
A public sector bank: the Government of India owns about 74.8% of its shares. Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank merged into it on 1 April 2020.
Led by MD & CEO Asheesh Pandey since 30 September 2025; he earlier was Executive Director of Bank of Maharashtra.
FY 2025-26 standalone net profit rose about 4% to ₹18,697 crore; Gross NPA fell to 2.82%.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit jumped 30.3% to ₹5,537 crore, loans grew 18.5% and Gross NPA improved to 2.42%.

timeline.t: Registered in Mumbai on 11 November, promoted by Seth Sitaram Poddar.
Mahatma Gandhi inaugurated the bank's head office building in Mumbai.
Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank merged into Union Bank of India.
Asheesh Pandey took charge as MD & CEO for three years.
Q2 FY27 profit rose 30.3% to ₹5,537 crore.

model.how: Union Bank earns mainly from the gap between interest on loans and interest paid on deposits, plus fees and treasury income. Most of its lending goes to retail, farm and MSME borrowers (the 'RAM' segments), along with corporate loans.
flow: Bank lends to people, farmers, MSMEs and companies

industry.regulator: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Government of India (as main owner)
points: The Government appoints the MD & CEO and Executive Directors of public sector banks.
Public sector banks merged into fewer, bigger banks in 2019–2020; Union Bank absorbed two banks.
Big theme for interviews: public sector banks have cut bad loans sharply and now earn strong profits.

numbers.say: Union Bank grew its profit 30% to ₹5,537 crore last quarter, with loans up 18.5% and bad loans down to 2.42%.

rivals.note: Among the public sector banks shown here, Union Bank's FY26 profit is behind SBI and Bank of Baroda and ahead of PNB. Canara Bank is not shown.

network.local: Union Bank has a wide branch network, with deep roots in the West (Mumbai) and, through Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank, in the South. New officers are often posted to rural and semi-urban branches.

employer.note: From the FY 2025-26 BRSR. Union Bank is one of India's large public sector employers.

csr.t: Union Bank's CSR runs mainly through the Union Bank Social Foundation, covering education and skills, healthcare and sanitation, livelihoods, the environment and disaster relief.

w.t: Margin of 2.86% is lower than private banks

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Amalgamation: Two or more companies combining into one. Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank merged into Union Bank in 2020.
glossary.IBPS: Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, which runs common recruitment exams for public sector banks.
glossary.RAM: Retail, Agriculture and MSME loans: the segments public sector banks are pushing for growth.

Personality, banking knowledge and HR questions

Finance.q: Union Bank's FY26 interest income fell but profit rose. How?
Finance.a: Net interest income fell about 1.5%, but lower bad-loan costs and other income lifted profit to ₹18,697 cr.

Finance.q: Gross NPA fell from 3.29% to 2.42% in a year. What drives that?
Finance.a: Recoveries, write-offs of old bad loans, fewer new defaults and faster loan growth.

Marketing.q: How would you attract young customers to Union Bank?
Marketing.a: Mobile-first account opening, student and first-salary accounts, and campaigns that mix a 100-year-old trusted name with modern features.

Marketing.q: Deposits are growing slower than loans. How would you raise deposits?
Marketing.a: Salary-account tie-ups, government and institutional accounts, and simple digital savings products with good service.

HR.q: How would you unite staff from three merged banks into one culture?
HR.a: Common training, mixed teams, fair postings and clear career paths. Union Bank had to do this after the 2020 merger.

Sales.q: Sell a Union Bank MSME loan to a small manufacturer.
Sales.a: Ask about working-capital needs, explain quick sanction and government-backed schemes simply, and close with a next step.

Operations.q: How can a public bank use automation to work faster?
Operations.a: Automate routine back-office tasks, central reconciliation and digital loan tracking. Union Bank is scaling up robotic process automation.

gd.t: Were public sector bank mergers a good idea?
gd.for: Bigger banks like Union Bank now earn strong profits and have stronger capital.
gd.against: Integrating staff and systems from three banks took years.

gd.t: Should the government reduce its stake in public sector banks?
gd.for: More private investors can bring efficiency.
gd.against: Government ownership supports rural and social banking goals.

avoid: Don't call Union Bank a private bank; the government owns about 74.8%.
Don't say Andhra Bank or Corporation Bank still exist; they merged into Union Bank in 2020.
Don't confuse Union Bank of India with United Bank of India, which merged into PNB in 2020.
Don't mix standalone (₹5,537 cr) and consolidated (₹5,781 cr) Q2 profit.
